title: Macro Insect Photography with Dewdrops
description: Close-up macro-style insect shots with dewdrops, suitable for biology textbooks, nature magazine covers, and stock photography.

prompt.main: extreme close-up macro photograph of a jewel beetle on a wet leaf at sunrise, intricate iridescent green and copper shell, tiny dewdrops on antennae, golden morning backlight, shallow depth of field, focus stacking, canon MP-E 65mm f/2.8 macro lens --ar 1:1 --v 6.1 --s 500

explained.why: Square ratio suits Instagram and product-style framing. Macro subjects are usually centered.
Balanced stylize for documentary + visual appeal. Pure photo (--style raw) also works well here.

tutorial.intro: Macro insect photography needs three things: real lens name, specific insect, specific lighting.
steps: Lens name: canon MP-E 65mm f/2.8 macro lens 鈥?naming a real lens is a cheat code for "real photo" feel.
Insect: jewel beetle on a wet leaf 鈥?specific insect, specific surface.
Detail cues: intricate iridescent green and copper shell 鈥?"iridescent" forces the metallic color shift.
Scale cues: tiny dewdrops on antennae 鈥?micro details that make it feel real.
Light: golden morning backlight, shallow depth of field, focus stacking 鈥?three professional photography terms.
tutorial.tips: Always name a real lens. "Canon MP-E 65mm" or "Laowa 100mm" works 10x better than "macro lens".

crossModel.midjourney: Use rewrite prompt. Add --style raw for more documentary feel.

crossModel.flux: Flux understands lens terminology natively. Use same prompt.
crossModel.dall_e: DALL-E 3 is good for macro. "An extreme close-up photograph of a jewel beetle..." works well.

faq.q: Why does my beetle look like a toy?
faq.a: You forgot the lens name. "Canon MP-E 65mm" makes MJ render the textures photographically.
Use "iridescent" + two color names (green and copper). "Iridescent" alone is too vague.
MJ v6.1 --style raw, or SDXL + JuggernautXL. Both handle nature realistically.
